"'''If I Ever Fall in Love'''" is a song by American [[Contemporary R&B|R&B]]-[[Soul music|soul]] quartet [[Shai (band)|Shai]]. It was released as their debut single in September 1992 from their debut album, ''[[...If I Ever Fall in Love]]'' (1992). The song, both written and produced by Carl "Groove" Martin, reached number two on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] in 1992 and peaked at number one on the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Hot R&B Singles]] chart. It spent eight weeks at number two on the Hot 100, which at the time was the [[List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones#Most weeks at number two|second-most number of weeks]] that a song held the position without topping the chart, behind [[Foreigner (band)|Foreigner]]'s "[[Waiting for a Girl Like You]]". The song was also their only top-40 hit in the [[UK Singles Chart|UK]], peaking at number 36.<ref name="ukchart">{{cite book | last1 = Warwick | first1 = Neil | last2 = Kutner | first2 = Jon | last3 = Brown | first3 = Tony | title = The Complete Book Of The British Charts | edition = 3rd | publisher = [[Omnibus Press]] | page = 977 | location = London | year = 2004 | isbn = 978-1-84449-058-5}}</ref>

"If I Ever Fall in Love" is a song by American R&B-soul quartet Shai. It was released as their debut single in September 1992 from their debut album, ...If I Ever Fall in Love (1992). The song, both written and produced by Carl "Groove" Martin, reached number two on the US Billboard Hot 100 in 1992 and peaked at number one on the Billboard Hot R&B Singles chart. It spent eight weeks at number two on the Hot 100, which at the time was the second-most number of weeks that a song held the position without topping the chart, behind Foreigner's "Waiting for a Girl Like You". The song was also their only top-40 hit in the UK, peaking at number 36.

"If I Ever Fall in Love" was covered in 1996 as a duet between British boy band [[East 17]] and singer-songwriter [[Gabrielle (singer)|Gabrielle]], completed with a backing track. Renamed "'''If You Ever'''" and released by [[London Records]], the cover peaked at number two on the [[UK Singles Chart]] and also peaked within the top 10 of the charts in Ireland and Sweden. The song received a platinum certification from the [[British Phonographic Industry]] in September 2019 for sales and streams exceeding 600,000.

The song was the first single from East 17's first Greatest Hits compilation, ''[[Around the World Hit Singles: The Journey So Far]]'' (1996), and was also the fourth single from Gabrielle's second [[Gabrielle (album)|self-titled album]] (1996). It was the highest-charting single from both aforementioned albums.

"If I Ever Fall in Love" was covered in 1996 as a duet between British boy band East 17 and singer-songwriter Gabrielle, completed with a backing track. Renamed "If You Ever" and released by London Records, the cover peaked at number two on the UK Singles Chart and also peaked within the top 10 of the charts in Ireland and Sweden. The song received a platinum certification from the British Phonographic Industry in September 2019 for sales and streams exceeding 600,000.

The song was the first single from East 17's first Greatest Hits compilation, Around the World Hit Singles: The Journey So Far (1996), and was also the fourth single from Gabrielle's second self-titled album (1996). It was the highest-charting single from both aforementioned albums.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: Kristy Barker from ''[[Melody Maker]]'' complimented "If You Ever" as "gorgeous" and "lovely".<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Kristy|last=Barker|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/nothingelseon/53732184341/|title=Singles|magazine=[[Melody Maker]]|date=October 26, 1996|page=47|access-date=May 28, 2024}}</ref> Kevin Courtney from ''[[Irish Times]]'' wrote, "The [[Walthamstow]] wideboys and the pirate patched [[Soul music|soul]] queen team up for this fairly run of the mill [[ballad]] [...]. At least it's a more appropriate pairing than [[Lulu (singer)|Lulu]] and [[Take That]] [on "[[Relight My Fire#Take That version|Relight My Fire]]"]. On the sleeve art, the numeral 17 has been replaced by the spelled out version, perhaps a sign that the Easties are making a subtle bid for a more "mature" audience. Why not go all the way and change their name to East Thirtysomething?"<ref>Courtney, Kevin (October 25, 1996). "Bohemian Rapping Fandango". ''[[Irish Times]]''.</ref>
sections.text: Kristy Barker from Melody Maker complimented "If You Ever" as "gorgeous" and "lovely". At least it's a more appropriate pairing than Lulu and Take That [on "Relight My Fire"]. On the sleeve art, the numeral 17 has been replaced by the spelled out version, perhaps a sign that the Easties are making a subtle bid for a more "mature" audience. Why not go all the way and change their name to East Thirtysomething?"
